second_check.explanation: The finding holds. I read the official text. Section 42 is headed "Trade secrets; definitions applicable to Secs. 42 to 42G" and begins "As used in this section and in sections 42A to 42G, inclusive, the following words...". It defines only "improper means", "misappropriation", "person" and "trade secret", and contains no remedies. The remedies the complaint claims are in other sections. § 42A covers injunctions: "Actual or threatened misappropriation may be enjoined upon principles of equity...". § 42B covers damages, including unjust enrichment, and § 42B(b) adds exemplary damages: "If willful and malicious misappropriation exists, the court may award exemplary damages in an amount not exceeding twice any award made under subsection (a)." § 42C covers fees: "The court may award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to the prevailing party if ... (iii) willful and malicious misappropriation exists." The proposition is correct under the Act, but the bare cite to § 42 points to the definitions section. In paragraph 118 the complaint writes the cite without "et seq." (the cease-and-desist letter uses "§ 42 et seq."). The right statute with the wrong section is closest to WRONG_CITATION_REAL_CASE. VERIFIED_MINOR_DEFECT would also be a defensible reading if a wrong section is treated like a wrong pin page. The correct cite is Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93, §§ 42A–42C.
